policy: suffix-match {password,token,api_key,ssn,card_number} recursively; card keeps last4; email stays
bug_report: Customer secrets are showing up readable in the log pipeline - a nested request payload reached the aggregator with its user_password and api_key values in plain text. Only a couple of top-level fields ever get scrubbed. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix redact so secrets stop leaking into logs, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: close the gaps in log-event scrubbing flagged by the compliance audit
decision_rationale: The audit found secrets leaking through redact - it only matched two exact top-level names. New rule: normalize each key (lowercase, non-alphanumerics to underscores) and treat it as sensitive when it ENDS WITH password, token, api_key, ssn or card_number, recursively through nested dicts and lists. Sensitive values become ***, except card numbers, which keep their last4 as ***1234 - support reconciles chargeback disputes by the last4. Email is explicitly NOT masked: support answers tickets by looking customers up by email, and scrubbing it broke that once before.
